title: Which Atoms Grab Electrons? Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A ball rolling downhill gives energy away, a dry sponge pulls in water, and a full glass cannot take one more drop. Atoms behave the same way when an electron arrives: some welcome it and release energy, some refuse it. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 3, Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties) Diya sprinkles salt and we ask what happened when each chlorine atom grabbed an electron from sodium.

You will see electron gain enthalpy defined piece by piece (X(g) + e- -> X-(g), negative when energy is released, positive when it must be supplied), then watch an electron drop into chlorine's empty place on the molecule bench while the energy bar falls to -349 kJ/mol, and see helium refuse one (+48 kJ/mol) because the new electron needs a brand new shell. NCERT Table 3.7 values build live for the halogens (F -328, Cl -349, Br -325, I -295) and the noble gases (He +48, Ne +116, Ar +96). We explain step by step why halogens release the most, and why fluorine releases less than chlorine (its small, crowded 2p shell repels the new electron). A worked example turns 3.55 g of chlorine atoms into 0.1 mol and 34.9 kJ released. Then the sign trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 33 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
